clips.title: pytest: everything you need to know about fixtures (intermediate) anthony explains #487
clips.why: Anthony Sottile, one of pytest's core maintainers, writes a first fixture and then adds setup and cleanup to it, which is the whole idea of this lesson.
look: The test names the fixture as a parameter, and pytest supplies the value.
How setup and cleanup live in one fixture function, with yield between them.
How this compares with separate setup and teardown functions.
clips.after: fcp's new API tests get every fake and every builder this way, so reading a test means reading its parameter list first.

clips.title: pytest: everything you need to know about fixtures (intermediate) anthony explains #487
clips.why: The same video, a short part on fixture scope: how often a fixture runs, once per test or once for the whole run.
look: The default scope: one call per test.
A wider scope, such as session, runs the fixture once and shares the result.
What changes when many tests share one fixture value.
clips.after: The slow database setup for fcp's API tests is a session-scoped fixture, so it is paid once per worker instead of once per test.

clips.title: pytest's parametrize (beginner - intermediate) anthony explains #027
clips.why: From the same maintainer: turning a copied test into one parametrized test, and naming each case so the report is readable.
look: The decorator names the parameters once and lists one tuple per case.
Each case appears as its own test in the output.
How to give the cases readable names instead of numbers.
clips.after: When a backend bug has several inputs, a parametrized test with clear case names is what you want to see in Nova's or a bug fixer's pull request.

practice.q: Mark this function so tests can ask for it by name.
practice.hint: The word this lesson uses for "setup a test asks for by name".
practice.why: @pytest.fixture registers the function under its own name, so any test with a trials_file parameter gets its return value.

practice.q: In Vitest you put shared setup in a beforeEach inside a describe. Where does the same setup go in pytest, so tests in several files can use it?

options.text: In a fixture in conftest.py, which each test asks for by naming it as a parameter.
options.why: conftest.py shares its fixtures with every test in its folder and below, and each test receives only the setup it names.

options.text: In a function called setup_each() at the top of every test file.
options.why: pytest has no hook named setup_each, so nothing calls it; you would have to call it from every test yourself.

options.text: In a test called test_000_setup, because pytest runs tests in alphabetical order.
options.why: Tests that depend on other tests break when run alone or in parallel. Setup belongs in fixtures.

practice.q: Run each case of this test once for every pair of values, like it.each.
practice.hint: Note pytest's spelling: no "e" after the "t".
practice.why: parametrize turns one function into one test per tuple, each with its own node ID in the report.

practice.q: Two tests write and read /tmp/trials.txt. They pass with pytest, but with pytest -n 4 they sometimes fail. What is the best fix?

options.why: That hides the shared state instead of removing it, and the tests still fail when run alone or in another order.

options.text: Let each test write its file under tmp_path, through a fixture, so no two tests share a path.
options.why: tmp_path is a fresh folder per test, so the tests no longer touch the same file, on any worker and in any order.

options.text: Add a sleep at the start of the second test so the first one finishes.
options.why: With workers in separate processes, timing is never guaranteed. A sleep makes the suite slower and still flaky.

practice.q: Put what happens on the second and third pytest --testmon runs in order.
items: The first run executes every test and writes .testmondata with the lines each test ran
You run it again without changes, and no tests run
You edit one line inside pass_rate
testmon compares the code with its record and selects only the tests that ran pass_rate
Those tests run, and the others are reported as deselected
practice.why: testmon needs one full run to learn which code each test touches. After that, every change selects only the tests that executed the changed code.
